title: All big fppf module sheaves and their canonical direct-image functors
statement: Work in [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be categories fibred in groupoids over $\mathit{Sch}/S$, and let $a:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$ be a functor over schemes [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Use the inherited big fppf sites, regular-function structure rings and their canonical common-universe lifts of [def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra]. Let $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{fppf}})$ be all structure-module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], without cartesian or quasi-coherent conditions. Abelian sheafification exists in the common ambient universe, inverts exactly locally bijective maps, and induces Mathlib's abelian module-sheaf structure [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. These module categories admit injective resolutions [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Precomposition with $a$ preserves sheaves. The canonical identification of structure rings is induced by the equality of the projections to schemes; define $a^*$ by literal precomposition using this identification. Its right adjoint $a_*$ is characterized up to unique compatible natural isomorphism by the adjunction; on a test $y$ it is compatible sections on $\mathcal D\times_{\mathcal C}(\mathit{Sch}/V)$, with base-change restrictions and the regular-function action. The right adjoint is additive. Define $R^qa_*$ for $q\in\mathbf N$ by applying $a_*$ to an injective resolution and taking degree-$q$ cohomology. No algebraicity, representability, finiteness, flatness or quasi-coherence hypothesis is imposed.
